title: Functional impact of GPTQ code disagreement and dense act-order stabilization
experiments_order: Experiment 1 (functional, no solves) completes before any Experiment 2 PPL evaluation

quantization.groups: consecutive group_size columns of the EXECUTION order (solver semantics; no static groups)

calibration.equivalence: Experiment 2 re-solves from the SAVED historical Hessians (same 128 C4 sequences, same order, same K=4 blocks); Hessian sha256 verified before every solve

experiment1.reference_model: BF16 original checkpoint (both models); activations captured once and shared by every variant

activations.gate_up: input of mlp.gate_proj (dense) / experts[e].gate_proj (MoE) = post-attention-norm hidden state (MoE: tokens routed to e under BF16 routing)
activations.down: actual input of down_proj in the BF16 forward (silu(gate x) * up x, BF16)
activations.routing: BF16 router: softmax(fp32) -> top-4 -> cast to bf16 (norm_topk_prob=False), as the HF block

experiment1.capture_validation: per-window NLL of the capture forward == historical BF16 baseline bitwise; MoE gate inputs == X[routed tokens] bitwise
experiment1.arithmetic: FP32 (TF32 off) on installed BF16 weights and captured BF16 activations; float64 accumulation
experiment1.E_func: ||(W_a - W_b) X||_F / ||W_BF16 X||_F over all (routed) tokens; reference = BF16 original weights
experiment1.E_mlp_dense: ||MLP_a(X) - MLP_b(X)||_F / ||MLP_BF16(X)||_F, X = captured MLP input, FP32 SiLU-GLU
experiment1.E_moe_expert: per expert: same as E_mlp on the expert's routed tokens (unweighted expert-level)
experiment1.E_moe_agg: ||sum_e w_te (E_a,e(x_t) - E_b,e(x_t))||_F / ||MoE_block_BF16(x)||_F (captured full block output incl. shared expert) over all 65,536 tokens; shared reference routing (selected experts + BF16 probabilities); secondary denominator: routed-only BF16 output
secondary: integer-code disagreement (dense all; MoE sampled 20 experts only)

pairs.secondary: all 10 grouping pairs; each config vs BF16

experiment1.ratios: R_X = MoE / dense for code, BF16, functional (per projection and MLP/MoE-block) and SD(log PPL); primary pair sets as above (exploratory cross-model comparison, not a causal decomposition)

classification.quantity: R_MLP = mean E_moe_agg over the 5 MoE primary pairs / mean E_mlp_dense over the 4 dense primary pairs (both pooled over the 4 layers by squared norms); R_code = 17.86 (runs_integer_code_mechanism, per projection gate 51.96 / up 51.57 / down 5.06); R_func_p per projection analogous to R_MLP
classification.F1: R_MLP <= 3 AND no projection with R_func_p >= 0.5 x R_code_p
classification.F3: otherwise, or projection-level ratios conflict (some R_func_p <= 0.25 R_code_p while another >= 0.5 R_code_p)
classification.note: the dense/MoE code ratio is on the 20 sampled MoE experts; functional ratios use all 240 experts

curvature.tensors: dense: all 12, 4 primary pairs; MoE: 20 sampled experts x 3 projections, 5 primary pairs
curvature.bins: 10 bins by (i) reference (ORIGINAL) execution position, (ii) calibration diag(H_ORIGINAL) quantile, (iii) held-out diag(X^T X) quantile; (i) and (ii) coincide up to reversal by construction of act-order
curvature.energy: diag approximation sum_j ||dW_:j||^2 Hheld_jj vs within-bin full quadratic form and the full tr(dW Hheld dW^T) (non-additivity reported)
curvature.split: quadratic-form split of ||dW X||^2 into code-flip elements, same-code (grid-only) elements, cross

policies.natural: argsort(diag H, descending) inside the solver (historical); reused after bitwise re-solve parity
policies.fixed: actorder_override = the ORIGINAL configuration's natural permutation for that projection (computed from the ORIGINAL Hessian); grouping Hessians, scales, zero-points, error feedback stay live. Cost: requires the reference calibration execution (one extra Hessian pass + argsort) and storage of 12 permutations; NOT reference-free
policies.bucketed: actorder_override = moe_calib.actorder_policy.bucketed_perm(own H, bits): float64 frexp mantissa truncated to bits significant bits (floor), descending key, ties by ascending column index (numpy stable argsort, CPU); primary bits = 8 (frozen after inspecting diag(H) only: logs/audit.json diag_inspection), exploratory [6, 10]; fixed power-of-two boundaries independent of observed min/max; reference-free
policies.disabled: gptq_quantize(actorder=False): original column order, groups = consecutive original columns

validation.A: natural re-solve from saved Hessians == historical BF16 weights bitwise (72 tensors) and natural PPL per-window == historical bitwise
validation.B: fixed path with each config's own natural permutation == natural output bitwise (72 tensors)
validation.C: bucketed permutation identical across 2 repeated computations and a clone of H; full bucketed solve repeated bitwise for one config
validation.D: disabled: info perm == arange, group == column // 128
validation.E: Hessian files sha256 == historical inventory; tokens == 65,536 per projection
validation.F: G20261115 == ORIGINAL bitwise within each policy
validation.G: only the 12 target tensors change; all other parameters digest-identical; restore to pristine
validation.H: repeat evaluation per-window NLL bitwise identical

primary_metrics: SD(PPL), SD(log PPL), CV over the 5 groupings per policy (ddof=1)
mean PPL, penalty vs BF16, mean change vs natural, best / worst, max pairwise diff
window-level paired mean NLL difference vs natural per grouping
secondary_metrics: code / level / BF16 / rel-Frobenius / act-order position / group / scale / zero disagreement vs the policy's ORIGINAL
E_mlp vs the policy's ORIGINAL on Experiment 1 activations

descriptors.code_stabilized: mean code disagreement (4 primary pairs) <= 0.5 x natural
descriptors.functional_stabilized: mean E_mlp (4 primary pairs) <= 0.5 x natural
descriptors.ppl_stabilized: R_SD <= 0.5 (descriptive only: 4 singleton perturbations + 1 exact null)
descriptors.quality_acceptable: mean PPL - mean natural PPL <= 0.10 x (mean natural PPL - BF16 PPL)
descriptors.hypothesis_C: code_stabilized AND functional_stabilized AND ppl_stabilized AND quality_acceptable

experiment2.statistical_limitation: 5 groupings = 4 singleton-row perturbations + 1 exact null; SDs are descriptive
